title: Differentially palmitoylated proteins in mitochondria from wild-type and ABHD10-knockout mice LC-MSMS
projectDescription: Palmitoylation is the only fully reversible post-translational lipid modification that impacts 10-20% of the human proteome, but its role during spermatogenesis remains enigmatic. In this study, through generating HA-tagged Abhd10 knock-in mice, Abhd10-null mice, and combining super-resolution fluorescence imaging and electron microscopy, we identified that the S-depalmitoylase ABHD10 is a mitochondrial matrix protein, specifically expressed in testis and is essential for male fertility. Abhd10 knockout mice manifest severe sperm motility defects accompanied by malformed mitochondrial sheaths of sperm. Strikingly, mitochondrial proteomic revealed that ABHD10 deficiency primarily disrupts respiratory chain complexes. Further, mass spectrometry-based mitochondrial acyl - biotin exchange (ABE) assays identified that ABHD10 catalyzes S-depalmitoylation of proteins involved in aerobic respiration and respiratory electron transport, particularly PDHX—key regulators of oxidative phosphorylation. In addition, ABHD10 could form complex with PDHX, thereby catalyzing its S-depalmitoylation. Overall, this work identifies S-depalmitoylase as a key determinant of male fertility and unveils the facilitating role of ABHD10-mediated S-depalmitoylation in oxidative phosphorylation.
sampleProcessingProtocol: 1. Differentially expressed proteins (WT vs KO testes) Testes (2-month-old mice) were lysed in SDT buffer (4% SDS, 100 mM DTT, 100 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0), boiled 3 min, sonicated, and treated with UA buffer containing detergent, DTT, and IAA. Proteins were digested overnight with trypsin (50:1, Promega, 37°C) and desalted using C18 StageTips. LC-MS/MS was performed on an Orbitrap Astral with Vanquish Neo UHPLC. DIA acquisition: survey scan 380–980 m/z, resolution 240,000, AGC target 500%, injection time 5 ms; DIA MS/MS 150–2000 m/z, 2 m/z isolation window, AGC 500%, injection time 3 ms, NCE 25, cycle time 0.6 s. Full MS in profile mode, DIA scans centroided.  2. Differentially expressed proteins (WT vs KO mitochondria) Mitochondria were isolated from brain, heart, liver, and testes using Proteintech kit PK10016. Tissues were homogenized in Isolation Reagent A (1:10 w/v) with Dounce homogenizer, layered on Isolation Reagent B, centrifuged 700 × g 10 min, supernatant centrifuged 10,000 × g 10 min to collect crude mitochondria. Pellets were washed, layered on C:D buffer (17:3), centrifuged 22,000 × g 10 min for purification, washed again (16,000 × g, 5 min). Purified mitochondria were extracted for MS analysis.  3. Differentially palmitoylated proteins (WT vs KO mitochondria) Mitochondria from 40 WT and 40 KO testes were lysed in 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 5 mM EDTA, 1% Triton X-100, protease inhibitors; rotated 1 h at 4°C, centrifuged 15,000 × g 15 min, supernatant precipitated by chloroform-methanol. Pellets were dissolved in 4% SDS buffer + 10 mM NEM, 37°C, 10 min; block buffer (20 mM NEM) added, rotated overnight at 4°C. After 3× CM precipitation, final pellet was split into +HAM (0.7 M hydroxylamine, 1 mM HPDP-biotin) and –HAM (50 mM Tris-HCl, 1 mM HPDP-biotin) tubes, incubated 1 h RT. Samples were CM precipitated, incubated with low-HPDP-biotin buffer, enriched with Streptavidin Magnetic Beads, washed, and palmitoylated peptides eluted with TCEP + 20 mM IAA (1 h RT). Peptides were dried, desalted (C18), vacuum-concentrated, dissolved in 0.1% FA for LC-MS/MS.
dataProcessingProtocol: DIA MS data were analyzed using DIA-NN 1.8.130,31. Database searches were conducted with results filtered to achieve a false discovery rate (FDR) of less than 1% at both peptide-spectrum-matched (PSM) and protein levels. Bioinformatics analyses were performed using Microsoft Excel and R statistical software, with hierarchical clustering and volcano plot generation executed in R.
